prompt: Create a polished landscape editorial illustration for DrainBear, a Hong Kong drain-service brand, to accompany an article comparing service needs. Wide horizontal 3:2 composition, bright white and pale blue architecture, navy and cobalt accents, dimensional folded-paper low-poly craft style, crisp physical lighting and plausible perspective. A friendly faceted WHITE POLAR BEAR technician in cobalt blue bib overalls and blue protective gloves is the consistent protagonist. One continuous editorial panorama with three clear spatial scenes, not UI cards and not a collage with borders: at left a compact clean Hong Kong apartment bathroom with toilet, basin and floor drain; middle a clean restaurant kitchen with stainless sink and a closed grease-trap access cover; at right a property courtyard with an accessible closed surface drain and a compact inspection equipment case. The bear calmly points out these three different work settings to a customer holding a phone. Building silhouettes subtly suggest Hong Kong in the background. No lettering, no numbers, no price, no badges, no watermarks. No dramatic flood, no open manhole, no person entering a drain, no technical cutaway pretending to specify actual plumbing. Editorial brand illustration only, not photographic evidence of a real job. Keep all subjects safely inside the frame with breathing space and simple readable silhouettes at mobile size.
